solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Standard transport restricts approved City trader's activity

indicators.note: to restrict something is to hem it in, so one piece is held inside another

blocks.note: stock as an adjective means standard, as in a stock reply
to bring something is to transport it
OK means approved, as in 'the plan got the OK'

explanation.surface: Standard transport arrangements hamper the work of a trader in the City of London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Transport' looks like part of the scene, but it is the verb to carry. 'The City' is London's financial district, so a City trader deals in shares.
explanation.definitionFit: Stockbroking is the business of buying and selling shares for clients, the typical work of a financial trader in London.

clue.text: Heard single by chap producing R&B hit

indicators.note: what is heard is taken by its sound rather than its spelling

blocks.note: sole means single or only, and is said the same as the spelling used here
a chap is a man

explanation.surface: A record producer hears a single by some bloke and turns it into a rhythm-and-blues hit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Single' looks like a record, matching the music surface, but it means sole, one only.
explanation.definitionFit: Soul Man was a famous 1967 song by Sam and Dave, a classic of rhythm and blues music.

clue.text: Yellow light over Florida city

blocks.note: or is the heraldic name for gold or yellow
to light on something, like a bird, is to land
O is the cricket scorer's abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: A yellow light shines above a city in Florida.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Light' is a verb here, as in alight or settle. In cricket an over is a set of six balls, scored as O.
explanation.definitionFit: Orlando is a large city in central Florida, home of Walt Disney World.

clue.text: Essential son rings those managing to supply musical instrument

definitions.note: plural answer, but 'keyboards' is used for one player's instrument, as in 'on keyboards'

indicators.note: to ring something is to encircle it, so the outer pieces go round another

blocks.note: key means essential, as in a key point
S is the abbreviation for son
a board is the group of people who manage a company

explanation.surface: A key son keeps company directors around him so they can provide an instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Essential son' is one piece split in two to form the ring, with the managers in the gap before its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: In band credits 'keyboards' names the electronic piano or synthesizer that a player performs on.

clue.text: Scottish detective using taxi around centre of Glasgow

indicators.note: turning something around makes it face the other way, so the letters run backwards
the centre of a word is its middle letter, the only one kept

blocks.note: Uber is the app-based taxi service
the fourth of seven letters sits in the middle

explanation.surface: A Scottish detective takes a cab around the middle of Glasgow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taxi' suggests CAB, which leads nowhere; the brand name UBER is what turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: Inspector John Rebus is the Edinburgh police officer in Ian Rankin's popular series of crime novels.

clue.text: Comparatively eccentric king that is right to embrace naked beauty?

indicators.note: something naked has had its outer layer stripped, so the first and last letters go
to embrace is to hold in one's arms, so one piece is wrapped round another

blocks.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king
beauty can be good LOOKS; stripping its outer letters leaves the inside
i.e. is the abbreviation of the Latin id est, that is
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: An odd king is happy to cuddle an unclothed beauty.
explanation.walkthrough: K, IE and R make the outside, with the stripped-down LOOKS inside after the K.
explanation.definitionFit: Kooky means strange or quirky, and its comparative form describes something more oddball than another.

clue.text: Turn one performs, it's free of charge

indicators.note: to perform is to act or work something out, so the letters are reworked into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A variety act does its turn for nothing, with no fee charged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Free of charge' reads as costing nothing, but it means having no electric charge.
explanation.definitionFit: A neutron is a subatomic particle in the nucleus that carries no electrical charge, unlike the proton.

clue.text: Article of clothing from Barmouth, dress that's ordered

indicators.note: something ordered has been put into a set arrangement, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone orders a dress from a shop in the Welsh seaside town of Barmouth.
explanation.walkthrough: Barmouth is a resort on the coast of Wales, chosen for its letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Bermuda shorts are knee-length casual shorts, a single garment despite the plural name.

clue.text: One supposedly never forgetting to approach shop for plant

blocks.note: proverbially, an elephant never forgets
to shop someone is to inform on them to the police, which is also to grass

explanation.surface: Someone with a perfect memory heads to a garden shop to buy a plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shop' is a British slang verb meaning to betray to the police; grass is the same slang, a grass being an informer.
explanation.definitionFit: Elephant grass is a tall African grass, also called napier grass, grown for fodder.

clue.text: Just as stormy heading off for Spain

indicators.note: the leading letter is taken away and something else is put in its place

blocks.note: squally weather is stormy, with sudden gusts
E is the international vehicle code for Spain (España)

explanation.surface: A ship sets off for Spain in conditions just as rough as before.
explanation.walkthrough: The S that heads SQUALLY is swapped for E.
explanation.definitionFit: Equally and 'just as' are interchangeable intensifiers in comparisons: equally good means just as good.

clue.text: Renewable energy source in book not many will read out

indicators.note: reading words out means voicing them, so the sound counts rather than the spelling

blocks.note: a bio, short for biography, is a kind of book
not many is few, and 'few will' contracts to few'll

explanation.surface: A book about green energy that few people will actually read.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the second part is spoken: FEW'LL is how 'few will' sounds in speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Biofuel is fuel made from plant or animal matter, which can be regrown, so it counts as renewable.

clue.text: Souvenir of soldiers filling police force occupations originally

indicators.note: a filling sits inside something else, like the jam in a sandwich
what comes originally comes first, so only the opening letter is used

blocks.note: the Met is London's Metropolitan Police
soldiers are the men, as against officers
first letter

explanation.surface: A keepsake from troops who join a police force and their various occupations.
explanation.walkthrough: The Met is the usual name for London's Metropolitan Police; soldiers as 'men' means the ranks rather than officers.
explanation.definitionFit: A memento is an object kept as a reminder of a person or event, much like a keepsake.

clue.text: Sort of pump, it purrs when activated

indicators.note: activating something sets it moving, so the letters are stirred into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A pump that makes a contented purring noise once you switch it on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sort of pump' is a fair definition because the answer is an adjective-like modifier: a stirrup pump.
explanation.definitionFit: A stirrup pump is a portable hand pump steadied by the foot in a loop, used for fighting small fires.

clue.text: Dog needing our hugs

indicators.note: to hug is to hold close, so the words hold the answer inside them

blocks.note: the letters run across the gap between the two words

explanation.surface: A dog that needs us to cuddle it.
explanation.walkthrough: Read through 'neeDING Our' to find a five-letter dog.
explanation.definitionFit: The dingo is the wild dog native to Australia, so it is a specific kind of canine.

clue.text: Concerning split in outwardly free American public votes

indicators.note: the outward part of a word is its two ends, so only the first and last letters are kept

blocks.note: re means concerning, as in a business letter
first and last letters
to rend is to tear or split
A is the abbreviation for American

explanation.surface: About a split among Americans who are free on the surface, shown in public ballots.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces simply follow one another; 'split' comes in the clue before the outer letters of free but is placed after them.
explanation.definitionFit: Referenda is the Latin-style plural of referendum, a direct vote by the whole electorate on one question.

clue.text: Sport Conservative finds tediously unoriginal

blocks.note: Formula One motor racing, with the roman numeral I for one
C is the abbreviation for Conservative

explanation.surface: A Conservative politician thinks some sport is dull and predictable.
explanation.walkthrough: The sport is Formula One, written with the numeral I. C for Conservative refers to Britain's Conservative Party.
explanation.definitionFit: Formulaic work follows a set pattern with no fresh ideas, so it is dull and derivative.

clue.text: One following triumph adored essentially

indicators.note: the essence of a thing is its core, so only the central letters are kept

blocks.note: a triumph is a success
the middle two of six letters

explanation.surface: A fan who followed a winner, really adoring them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One following' looks like a fan, but it means whoever comes after.
explanation.definitionFit: A successor is the person who comes after another in a job or title, taking over the role.

clue.text: Dismiss bank employee

blocks.note: first meaning: to discharge someone from the armed forces in disgrace
second meaning: the person at a counter who handles money

explanation.surface: Fire a bank worker.
explanation.walkthrough: The verb sense is military: an officer is cashiered when thrown out for misconduct.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb for discharging in disgrace and a noun for a teller who pays out money.

clue.text: Awfully angered?

indicators.note: something done awfully is done badly, so the letters are mangled into another order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and the definition: rearranged letters of the second word, and a description of fury.
explanation.definitionFit: To be enraged is to be made extremely furious, which is what being terribly cross amounts to.

clue.text: Surround European wearing finest clothes

indicators.note: whoever wears clothes is inside them, so one piece is put within another
to clothe something is to cover it all round, confirming that the outer piece wraps the inner

blocks.note: the finest is the best
E is the abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: Crowd round a European dressed in their very best clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Finest clothes' reads as Sunday best; BEST is the clothing and E is the wearer inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To beset is to attack or hem in from all sides, so it can mean to surround.

clue.text: Sick bishop inspiring one about upsetting germs

indicators.note: to inspire is literally to breathe in, so one piece is taken inside another
to upset is to tip over, and in a down clue that turns the letters upside down

blocks.note: sick means ill
I is the roman numeral one
ca. is the abbreviation of circa, about
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: An ailing bishop breathes in a fellow cleric's nasty germs.
explanation.walkthrough: The bishop does not literally enclose anything: 'sick bishop' is one string that takes the inner pieces in its gap, and the whole is then read from bottom to top.
explanation.definitionFit: Bacilli are rod-shaped bacteria, some of which cause disease, so they are classic germs.

clue.text: Test out very new hat

indicators.note: out can mean wrong or disordered, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
so means very, as in so good
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: Try on a brand-new hat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Test out' reads as a phrasal verb, but 'out' works on 'Test' alone.
explanation.definitionFit: A Stetson is a wide-brimmed cowboy hat, named after its American maker John B. Stetson.

clue.text: Celebrate newspaper mostly

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

blocks.note: A British Sunday newspaper

explanation.surface: Mark an occasion with a newspaper, more or less.
explanation.walkthrough: The Observer is the Sunday paper published alongside the Guardian; lose its last R.
explanation.definitionFit: To observe a festival or anniversary is to keep or mark it formally, much like celebrating it.

clue.text: Record from idol or newcomer on the rise?

indicators.note: taking something from within the words means the letters lie inside them
rising in a down entry means reading upwards, so the letters go backwards

blocks.note: the letters run across the ends of three words

explanation.surface: A record by a pop idol or an up-and-coming new act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Record' suggests a disc, matching the rising star, but it is the verb to register. Read 'idoL OR NEwcomer' backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To enrol someone is to enter their name on an official list or register, which is to put them on record.

clue.text: Dim relative runs boxing academy at first

indicators.note: to box something is to put it in a case, so one piece is enclosed by others
what comes at first is the opening letter, the only one used

blocks.note: an uncle is a relative
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
first letter

explanation.surface: A dull-witted relation runs a boxing club that starts out as an academy.
explanation.walkthrough: UNCLE and R side by side take A in between them. 'Dim' wants to mean stupid; here it means faint or vague.
explanation.definitionFit: Something dim is hard to make out, which is what unclear means: indistinct or vague.

clue.text: Del Boy's friend set off

blocks.note: first meaning: the dim road sweeper pal of Del Boy in the BBC sitcom Only Fools and Horses
second meaning: to cause something to start, such as an alarm

explanation.walkthrough: Del Boy Trotter is the market trader hero of Only Fools and Horses, a much-loved British TV comedy; his friend is called Trigger.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb the word means to activate or start, as when a motion sensor sets an alarm going.

clue.text: Flipping half-heartedly spots key area in map books

indicators.note: doing something half-heartedly means losing some of its heart, so a central letter goes
flipping something over turns it the other way, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: to spot is to see, so spots gives SEES, which loses one middle E
Alt is a key on a computer keyboard
A is the abbreviation for area

explanation.surface: Someone idly flicks through atlases, spotting a key region on the maps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Key' points to a map's legend, but it is a keyboard key. The pieces run backwards once joined.
explanation.definitionFit: An atlas is a bound collection of maps, so a book of maps; the answer is its plural.

clue.text: Liking bet that involves large stake ultimately

indicators.note: to involve is to wrap up or include, so one piece is enclosed within another
ultimately means in the end, so only the final letter is used

blocks.note: a bet is a prediction of the outcome
L is the abbreviation for large
last letter

explanation.surface: A fondness for a wager that puts a big sum on the line.
explanation.walkthrough: L and E join, then go inside PREDICTION after its fifth letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A predilection is a special preference or fondness for something, a synonym of a liking.
